newsitem.title: CANADA: Bre-X stock falls amid gold play dispute.
newsitem.headline: Bre-X stock falls amid gold play dispute.

text.p: The stock of Canada's Bre-X Minerals Ltd. fell sharply in heavy trading Friday after new uncertainty surfaced over the ownership of its multibillion-dollar Indonesian gold property.

Bre-X, operator of the Busang gold property, touted as one of the world's richest deposits, saw its stock drop after a Canadian newspaper reported the company faced potential legal snags with an Indonesian partner and the country's government.

Bre-X shares on the Toronto Stock Exchange were down C$2.35 to C$24.45 with 5.9 million shares changing hands after a trading halt to allow the company to explain its position was lifted. The junior gold firm's Nasdaq-listed shares fell $1.72 to $18.

The company, responding to a story Friday in the Toronto Globe and Mail newspaper, said its Indonesian legal adviser told it that claims of one of its Indonesian partners to a 10 percent stake in Busang's richest zones were without merit.

The partner, PT Krueng Gasui, has a 10 percent stake in Busang I, known as the central zone, and said it was entitled to a similar stake in Busang II and Busang III, the southeast and northwest zones.

The Indonesian government said the partner was considering legal action, reported the newspaper, which added that Indonesia would not sign a Contract of Work (CoW), which is required for further development, until outstanding issues were resolved.

Bre-X also said another issue reported, regarding an alleged breach of the Contract of Work for the central zone, was based on a misunderstanding by the Indonesian partner over how Bre-X acquired its interest in PT Westralian Atan Minerals of Australia, the former owner of the Busang land.
Bre-X said it had held discussions with senior Indonesian government officials regarding the matter and was confident the it would get its permits for Busang II and III.
Michael Fowler, analyst with Levesque Beaubien Geoffrion, said the entrance of players seeking claims to Busang's richest deposits came as no surprise.

Analysts have estimated Busang's total gold potential to be anywhere between 50 million and 100 million ounces. Drilling has indicated the gold harboured in the southeast zone dwarfs that in the central zone.

"The basic thing about this is you've got a C$5.5- or C$6-billion ($4 billion or $4.4-bilion) ore deposit sitting right there and people want a part of the pie. That's what it comes down to," Fowler said.
He said that, while he did not have all of the details on the claims, he could see no reason why the 10 percent partner in the central zone would have a claim on the southeast zone.
